candidates.label: Tyre archaeological site (Sour)
candidates.support: Tyre, on the coast of the South Governorate of Lebanon, is undisputed in identity and location; the Digital Atlas of the Roman Empire's coordinate for the site and Wikidata's coordinate agree closely.

summary.text: Tyre was, per UNESCO, a major Phoenician city that dominated ancient Mediterranean seaborne trade, founding colonies such as Carthage. Jesus withdrew into the region of Tyre and Sidon, and there healed the daughter of a Gentile woman whom Mark calls 'a Greek, a Syrophoenician by race'; on his final journey to Jerusalem Paul's ship put in at Tyre, where he stayed with disciples for seven days before continuing to Ptolemais.

otConnections.note: Ezekiel pronounces judgment against Tyre because the city gloated over Jerusalem's fall ('Aha! She is broken!'), declaring that many nations will come up against Tyre 'as the sea causes its waves to come up.'
Hiram, king of Tyre, supplies Solomon with cedar timber for the building of the Jerusalem temple; UNESCO also states that Hiram supplied the temple's material and architect.
